notes: Phonon-2 for LiteRT (litert-community/Phonon-2): FermionResearch/Phonon-2 (revision 3e6ab3a8, CC-BY-4.0) keeps the architecture and tokenizer of nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 (a 24-layer encoder and a TDT decoder) and stores the encoder's linear weights as five values per output row and the other large weights as 6-bit tables; these files expand them to float16 (the f16 forms, for the GPU and the NPU) or int8 (the i8 forms, for the CPU, quantized with ai-edge-quantizer 0.10.0), exported with litert-torch 0.9.4 into raw LiteRT graphs: an encoder per window length (the first release: three files, 10 / 20 / 30 s; the update: one file with the seven signatures enc5 / enc7.5 / enc10 / enc15 / enc20 / enc25 / enc30, in three forms: f16, f16 compiled ahead of time for the SM8850, i8; a window runs in the smallest length that holds it, with a valid-length mel mask), a log-mel graph per window length and one int8 TDT decoder. Text = the token ids decoded with the repo's tokenizer.json (repeated ids kept). Accuracy is WER against reference P_ii (transformers 5.20.2 ParakeetForTDT in float32 with the weights read out of Phonon-2's container, the same windows with a valid-length mask, the same greedy TDT decoding), with both the open-asr-leaderboard formula (L) and jiwer (J); sets from hf-audio/open-asr-leaderboard @ de79e57a. This file: phonon2_mel_20s.tflite (2,252,068 B), windows up to 20 s; the log-mel front end for windows up to 20 s on the CPU (pre-emphasis 0.97, STFT n_fft 512 / win 400 / hop 160, Slaney mel 128, log, per-window normalization over the valid frames; no weights); the same bytes as litert-community/parakeet-ultra's parakeet_ultra_mel_20s.tflite (Hub LFS sha256). artifact_sha256 = (source mel20.tflite) = the bytes the runs pushed (the phone's sha256 read-back MATCH in each frame) = the Hub LFS sha256 and size after the update's upload (litert-community/Phonon-2 commit af7585184bcd1b6e567ce5497440065ec51220b3, 25 files; 25 / 25 SAME). Pixel 11 Pro: the runs the card reads that load this file, and nothing else — CPU: S4 h2cpu_s4_all7, S4 p1cpu_int8f_s4; GPU: S4 f6gpu_s4_b1, S4 f6gpu_s4_b2, timing f2t_gpu_all. Runners: ultra_asr_runner_p, ultra_asr_runner_p6, ultra_asr_runner_p7. Not records: the other --pipeline setting of each A/B pair (the card quotes its RTF), the earlier runs of the same forms, the two-accelerator forms (not published), the card's usage-block runs and the Mac rows. The Pixel 11 Pro's per-window encoder figures (491.1 ms and the shorter graphs) come from a four-signature f16 file that is not published (run f2t_gpu_all, enc_all_fp16ws.tflite): no record; the same run's decoder and mel graphs are the published bytes and have their records. Records written.
